title: Go-live staffing simulator + KPI lighthouse (runbook draft)
summary: Working draft: interactive staffing simulator paired with KPI lighthouse (key triggers) to guide staffing + escalation decisions during phased rollouts. Focused on first 72 hours and first 30 days after initial traffic ramp. Intentionally lightweight — meant for ops leads to run quick sims and decide on on-call/handoff cadence.
assumptions:
- Initial canary user cohort = 5% of target launch traffic.
- Average request payload size = 1.2 KB.
- Median latency SLO (p50) target = 120ms for text-generation routes; p95 target = 400ms.
- Baseline error rate pre-launch = 0.2% (non-service errors).
- Each on-call engineer can triage ~10 escalations/hour (avg) during peak.
- Support agents can handle ~25 tickets/day for launch-specific issues with templated responses.
simulation_scenarios:
1) Smooth ramp: 0->100% over 72 hours with 95th percentile below SLO — minimal escalation.
2) Latency spike: sudden p95 increase to 800ms at 24h due to autoscale lag — requires urgent infra + routing changes.
3) Gradual error lift: error rate moves from 0.2% to 1.5% across 48h (model degradation / infra mismatch).
4) Traffic burst: 3x expected traffic over 6 hours (external marketing) — capacity breach.

Notes: run each scenario with 'fast-fix' (canary rollback, traffic-shed, model fallback) and 'slow-fix' timelines (engineering patch + cache warm-up).
staffing_matrix_guidance:
- Roles: Launch lead (1), SRE on-call (1 primary + 1 secondary), Model ops (1), Product ops coordinator (1), Support triage rotation (1 per 8-hour shift).
- For first 72h: recommend 24/7 coverage: 3 engineers per 24h (distributed) + 2 support agents.
- Week 1: scale down to business-hours heavy coverage + on-call nights (1 engineer), increase support to 3 agents as adoption grows.
- Escalation latency target: first ack within 15 minutes for P0; initial investigation in 60 minutes.
kpi_lighthouse:
Primary KPIs to watch live:
- Request rate (rps) by route
- P50 / P95 latency by model & route
- Error rate (5xx and model-empty-resp)
- Token consumption per minute (cost signal)
- Autoscale events / queue length (backend metric)
- Fallback rate (percent of requests served by fallback model or region)

Threshold triggers:
- Amber: p95 > 2x SLO for 5min OR error rate > 0.8% sustained 10min
- Red: p95 > 3x SLO OR error rate > 2% sustained 5min OR queue length > capacity threshold

Actions mapped to triggers:
- Amber -> Notify SRE on-call, enable temporary traffic shaping to canaries, open triage channel
- Red -> Run immediate fallback, engage on-call engineering war room, notify CS & leadership, initiate rollback plan
prelaunch_checklist: Verify canary routing and fallback policies in Console (route ids + model pins)
Confirm autoscaler policies for Dedicated pools (min/max/GPU headroom)
Run dry-run load test at 1.5x expected peak with KV cache warmed
Validate alert hooks (PagerDuty, Slack channel, Console alert endpoints)
Pre-create incident templates (P0/P1) and support canned responses
Ensure playbook links are in on-call rotation docs and that backups are assigned
Confirm cost-visibility dashboards with token-level attribution for top 10 customers
Dry-run canary rollback and model toggle in staging with test token
postmortem_todo:
If any amber/red event occurs during ramp:
- Capture timeline (who, what, when) within 4 hours
- Snapshot Console logs, cost spike charts, and KV cache status
- Do an immediate small retro (within 48h) focusing on detection-to-action times
- Full postmortem w/ corrective action items due in 7 days

quick_run_instructions:
How to run a quick staffing sim (product-ops):
1) Open the attached spreadsheet template (linked in artifacts).
2) Input expected peak RPS and canary % (default 5%).
3) Select scenario (smooth / latency_spike / burst).
4) Simulator outputs recommended engineering headcount and escalation timeline (use as advisory).

Notes: the simulator is conservative — plan 15-25% more staff for external events you can't control.
